lesson_title: Your Arm Is a Bad Lever on Purpose
hook_text: Your biceps pulls six times harder than the brick in your hand. Why would a body be built like that?
clip_script: Lift a brick with a bent arm. Your elbow is the pivot. Your muscle pulls just in front of it. The brick is far out in your hand. Effort in the middle: a third-class lever. It never makes you stronger. Your muscle pulls several times harder than the brick weighs. Terrible deal? Watch your hand. The muscle shortens a couple of centimetres and your hand flies up thirty. Third-class levers buy speed and reach: fishing rods, brooms, cricket bats, tweezers, and every limb you own. Now the opposite. A wheelbarrow: wheel is the pivot, bricks in the middle, hands at the end. Load in the middle: second class. It always makes you stronger, and more so the closer the bricks sit to the wheel. Nutcrackers, bottle openers, office punches. One question sorts every lever on Earth: what is in the middle?
visual_style: Whiteboard forearm with elbow pivot and a short muscle arrow beside a long brick arrow, then a wheelbarrow with bricks sliding towards the wheel as the handle arrow shrinks.
mood: Surprising and friendly; the body's design makes sense by the end.
pacing: Hook on the arm, quick reveal of speed, flip to the wheelbarrow, one-question finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and classify five tools in your kitchen by what is in the middle.
